chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah and Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khald Al-Barqi, from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah Al-Hasani Al-Alawi, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Hakam Al-Nakha'i, from Kathir ibn Shihab Al-Harithi, who said:

While we were sitting with the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) in Al-Rahbah, Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) appeared. He said: Ali (peace be upon him) smiled until his teeth became visible.
Then he said: Indeed, Allah mentioned a people and said, 'Neither did the heavens weep over them, nor the earth, nor were they granted respite.'
I swear to He who split the grain and created the living beings, that this one will be killed and the heavens and the earth will weep over him.

key_terms.بَرَأَ النَّسَمَةَ: He who created the living beings/souls
key_terms.فَلَقَ الْحَبَّةَ: He who split the grain (a divine attribute)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the heavens and earth weeping for Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam Ali (a.s.) smiles upon seeing Imam Husayn (a.s.) and contrasts the cosmic indifference described in Surah Az-Zukhruf (44:29) with the profound grief the heavens and earth will shed for Husayn’s martyrdom. This highlights the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt, whose suffering elicits a divine response from creation itself, affirming the reality of the 'Weeping of the Heavens' as a sign of their innocence and high rank.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 19. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, and from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid Al-Barqi, from ‘Abdil ‘Aďīm ibn ‘Abdillāh Al-Ḥasani Al-‘Alawy, from Ḥasan ibn Ḥakam Al-Nakha’i, from Kuthayr ibn Shihāb Al-Ḥārithi, who said:

(One day) while we were sitting with the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) in Ruḥbah, Ḥusain (a.s.) entered. (When the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) saw him), he smiled in a way that his teeth could be seen.

Then he (the Commander of the Believers (a.s.)) said: Allāh has mentioned some people in the Qur’an by saying, “Neither did the heavens weep over them, nor the earth, nor were they granted respite” [44:29].
I swear to He, who split the grain and created the living beings, that he (Ḥusain (a.s.)) will be killed and the heavens and the earth will weep over him.
